speaker: MONICA
line: There's nothing to tell! He's just some guy I work with!

speaker: JOEY
line: C'mon, you're going out with the guy! There's gotta be something wrong with him!

speaker: CHANDLER
line: All right Joey, be nice. So does he have a hump? A hump and a hairpiece?

speaker: PHOEBE
line: Wait, does he eat chalk?

speaker: MONICA
line: Just, 'cause, I don't want her to go through what I went through with Carl- oh!

speaker: ROSS
line: Hi.

speaker: JOEY
line: This guy says hello, I wanna kill myself.

speaker: MONICA
line: Are you okay, sweetie?

speaker: ROSS
line: I just feel like someone reached down my throat, grabbed my small intestine, pulled it out of my mouth and tied it around my neck.

speaker: CHANDLER
line: Cookie?

speaker: MONICA
line: Carol moved her stuff out today.

speaker: JOEY
line: Ohh.

speaker: CHANDLER
line: Could this day BE any more depressing?

speaker: PHOEBE
line: Give her a break, Ross. It's tough when a marriage ends.

speaker: ROSS
line: No, I don't want a break! We were on a break! Well, actually, that happens later in season three. Right now, I just want to be married again!

speaker: CHANDLER
line: And I just want a million dollars!

speaker: MONICA
line: Rachel?!

speaker: RACHEL
line: Oh God Monica, hi! Thank God! I went to your apartment, but you weren't there, and some guy with a big hammer told me you'd be here!

speaker: JOEY
line: Hey, how you doin'?

speaker: MONICA
line: Joey, stop hitting on her! She's hysterical!

speaker: RACHEL
line: I just realized I'm wearing a wedding dress and I didn't marry Barry!

speaker: ROSS
line: I'm supposed to attach bracket A to slot B, but this Allen wrench is completely stripped!

speaker: JOEY
line: Don't look at me, Ross. When I need furniture, I find a nice recliner on the curb.

speaker: CHANDLER
line: Could that Allen wrench BE any more useless? I mean honestly, who designs these Swedish torture devices?

speaker: ROSS
line: What is this? This is an extra piece! I have leftover parts!

speaker: JOEY
line: Dude, it's a spare. Like an extra kidney.

speaker: ROSS
line: You don't have spare parts when building a velociraptor skeleton at the museum! Paleontology requires absolute anatomical fidelity!

speaker: CHANDLER
line: And living with you requires earplugs.

speaker: ROSS
line: Okay, we're gonna lift and turn! Ready?

speaker: CHANDLER
line: I am ready to drop this sofa directly on my foot.

speaker: ROSS
line: Lift... and turn! Pivot! Pivot!

speaker: CHANDLER
line: Shut up! Shut up! Shut up!

speaker: ROSS
line: PIVOT!

speaker: CHANDLER
line: I don't think it can pivot any more without violating the laws of three-dimensional Euclidean physics!

speaker: ROSS
line: It's wedged. It is permanently wedged.

speaker: JERRY
line: You know what I noticed about the ketchup bottle?

speaker: GEORGE
line: What about the ketchup bottle?

speaker: JERRY
line: Nobody ever hits the bottom. They tap the neck. Why do they tap the neck? Is there an aerodynamic advantage to tapping the neck?

speaker: GEORGE
line: Jerry, I have bigger problems than condiment aerodynamics! Susan wants me to look at wedding invitations! High-grade vellum with embossed calligraphy!

speaker: JERRY
line: Vellum? That sounds fancy.

speaker: GEORGE
line: It is fancy! And expensive! Why do we need vellum? Who is inspecting the paper quality of an invitation? You look at it, you see the date, you throw it in the recycling!

speaker: ELAINE
line: You are not going to believe who I just saw on 55th street.

speaker: JERRY
line: The Soup Nazi?

speaker: ELAINE
line: Yes! The queue was around the block! I waited forty-five minutes for turkey chili!

speaker: GEORGE
line: Did you follow the ordering protocol? You have to step to the left! If you don't step to the left, he yells at you!

speaker: ELAINE
line: I stepped to the left! I had my exact change ready!

speaker: KRAMER
line: Jerry! The air conditioning! It's gone!

speaker: JERRY
line: What do you mean it's gone?

speaker: KRAMER
line: The compressor blew! It's ninety-eight degrees in my living room! My butter is melting on the counter!

speaker: GEORGE
line: These pretzels are making me thirsty!

speaker: JERRY
line: Kramer, why do you have butter on your counter?

speaker: KRAMER
line: Because room-temperature butter spreads evenly, Jerry! It's an artisanal culinary technique!

speaker: ELAINE
line: Kramer, you're eating melted salted butter with a spoon.

speaker: KRAMER
line: Giddyup!

speaker: CHANDLER
line: Could this coffee BE any hotter? I think my tongue just suffered second-degree burns.

speaker: JOEY
line: Hey, how you doin'? You can't complain about coffee when it's free.

speaker: ROSS
line: It's not free, Joey. Monica paid for it.

speaker: MONICA
line: Exactly! And I expect everyone to use coasters! We are civilized human beings who respect treated wooden surfaces!

speaker: PHOEBE
line: You know, in my past life in Prague, coasters were considered bad karma. We rested our wooden chalices directly on the mud floor.

speaker: RACHEL
line: Guys, look at this magazine. It says that ninety percent of men can't commit to a relationship because of deep-seated childhood anxieties.

speaker: ROSS
line: That is statistically unsubstantiated! Paleontological evidence indicates hominids formed lifelong pair-bonds for communal offspring defense!

speaker: CHANDLER
line: Yes, and nothing says romantic pair-bonding like dragging a woolly mammoth by its tusks into a cave.

speaker: JOEY
line: Did somebody say mammoth sandwich? Because I'm starving. Joey doesn't share food, but I would share mammoth.

speaker: RACHEL
line: Joey, woolly mammoths went extinct twelve thousand years ago.

speaker: JOEY
line: Well, whose fault is that? Probably Ross and his dinosaur friends.

speaker: ROSS
line: We were on a break from hunting! I mean, we were never hunting dinosaurs! Humans and dinosaurs never coexisted!

speaker: CHANDLER
line: Could your defense mechanism BE any more predictable?

speaker: SHELDON
line: Technically speaking, Ross Geller's assertion regarding hominid pair-bonding ignores evolutionary sociobiology.

speaker: LEONARD
line: Sheldon, Ross is a fictional character in an alternate sitcom dimension.

speaker: SHELDON
line: That is irrelevant. Scientific accuracy must prevail across all multi-verse configurations! Bazinga!

speaker: HOWARD
line: Speaking of multi-verses, my mother called three times asking if I want brisket or kugel for dinner.

speaker: RAJ
line: Howard, you are a thirty-year-old aerospace engineer. You should be cooking your own chicken biryani.

speaker: PENNY
line: Hey guys, what's up? Sheldon, why are there seven whiteboard equations blocking the hallway?

speaker: SHELDON
line: Penny, I am deriving the quantum wave function of a particle confined within a one-dimensional potential well.

speaker: PENNY
line: Right, and I am deciding whether to drink white wine or red wine with pizza.

speaker: LEONARD
line: Red wine goes better with pepperoni, Penny.

speaker: SHELDON
line: Only if you disregard the tannin oxidation process, Leonard. Honestly, your palate is pedestrian. Bazinga!

speaker: HOWARD
line: I once built an automated cocktail dispenser for zero gravity. It exploded in the test vacuum chamber.

speaker: RAJ
line: It didn't just explode, Howard. It soaked the Dean of Engineering in synthetic gin.

speaker: JERRY
line: What is the deal with airline peanuts? Have you ever tried to open one of those miniature nitrogen-flushed foil pouches at thirty thousand feet?

speaker: GEORGE
line: Jerry, I can't even open a childproof aspirin bottle without weeping! My hands are delicate! I was born for velvet robes, not manual labor!

speaker: ELAINE
line: George, you worked as an assistant to the traveling secretary for the Yankees. You handed out promotional baseball caps!

speaker: GEORGE
line: That was high-stress logistics, Elaine! High-stress!

speaker: KRAMER
line: Jerry! You've gotta invest in my new business venture!

speaker: JERRY
line: What business venture, Kramer?

speaker: KRAMER
line: The tie-dispenser! You go to a restaurant, you spill marinara on your necktie—bam! A vending machine dispenses a fresh silk four-in-hand tie!

speaker: GEORGE
line: Nobody wears ties to restaurants anymore!

speaker: KRAMER
line: Giddyup! The corporate elite wears ties, George! The movers and the shakers!

speaker: ELAINE
line: These pretzels are making me thirsty!

speaker: JERRY
line: See, that's observational comedy. Simple, direct, undeniably neurotic.

speaker: GEORGE
line: I am neurotic, Jerry! I am the king of neurosis! If neurosis were an Olympic event, I'd take home the silver medal because I'd choke on the gold!

speaker: CHANDLER
line: Could this multiverse BE any more crowded?

speaker: SHELDON
line: According to the Everett many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics, this superposition of comedic protagonists was inevitable.

speaker: JOEY
line: How you doin', Sheldon? You look like you need a slice of pepperoni pizza.

speaker: SHELDON
line: I do not consume unsolicited carbohydrates from strangers. Furthermore, your posture suggests deficient lumbar support.

speaker: GEORGE
line: You think you have problems? My parents are moving into a retirement community in Florida, and they expect me to drive the U-Haul!

speaker: CHANDLER
line: I would rather assemble fifty Swedish flat-pack entertainment units than drive a U-Haul to Florida.

speaker: KRAMER
line: Florida! The sunshine state! The citrus groves! I knew a guy in Boca Raton who trained pelicans to retrieve lost golf balls!

speaker: ROSS
line: Pivot the golf balls! Pivot!

speaker: MONICA
line: Who left this coffee mug without a coaster on the mahogany table?!

speaker: SHELDON
line: It was not I. My coaster placement adheres to strict Cartesian coordinates.

speaker: JERRY
line: And so the universe folds in upon itself, one sarcastic punchline at a time.

speaker: LEONARD
line: Penny said she's having trouble with her car engine again. I thought I might go over and take a look.

speaker: SHELDON
line: Why? Are you suddenly credentialed in internal combustion mechanics, or is this merely another desperate attempt to exchange unreciprocated romantic affection for amateur vehicular repair?

speaker: LEONARD
line: It's just a loose fan belt, Sheldon.

speaker: SHELDON
line: Technically, Leonard, your probability of repairing that engine without inducing catastrophic mechanical failure is less than twelve percent.

speaker: HOWARD
line: Gentlemen! Feast your eyes on the latest piece of NASA waste management hardware!

speaker: RAJ
line: Howard, please don't describe the zero-gravity toilet before we eat dinner.

speaker: SHELDON
line: Howard, an engineering feat is merely physics applied by individuals who lack the intellectual rigor to solve differential equations.

speaker: HOWARD
line: Hey! I have a Master's degree in engineering from MIT!

speaker: SHELDON
line: Yes, and my sister has a swimming certificate from the YMCA. Both are equally irrelevant in the realm of quantum electrodynamics.

speaker: LEONARD
line: Sheldon, be nice.

speaker: SHELDON
line: I am being nice! I didn't mention that his belt buckle is an aesthetic catastrophe. Bazinga!

speaker: SHELDON
line: I have discovered a profound flaw in the string theory compactification calculations published by the Cambridge group.

speaker: LEONARD
line: Oh really? Did you account for the Calabi-Yau manifold curvature?

speaker: SHELDON
line: Of course I accounted for the manifold curvature! What do you take me for, an experimentalist?

speaker: RAJ
line: He has a point, Leonard. You do play with lasers all day.

speaker: HOWARD
line: Lasers are cool! Lasers can burn a hole through a tungsten carbide plate!

speaker: SHELDON
line: Lasers are applied photonics. Children play with laser pointers in cinema auditoriums. Theoretical physics, on the other hand, decodes the fundamental fabric of spacetime.

speaker: LEONARD
line: Could you pass the mustard, Dr. Fabric-of-Spacetime?

speaker: SHELDON
line: Only if you acknowledge that the yellow mustard in question exhibits non-Newtonian fluid dynamics when subjected to shear stress.

speaker: PENNY
line: Hey guys! What are we talking about?

speaker: SHELDON
line: We are discussing the thermodynamic viscosity of condiments.

speaker: PENNY
line: Cool, I have no idea what that means. Did you fix my car, Leonard?

speaker: SHELDON
line: He did not, Penny. Because Leonard's understanding of machinery is strictly theoretical, much like his dating life. Bazinga!
